thread:
simon: Heads-up — noticed some customers hitting stuck goroutines in our Go SDK when cancelling streaming requests over HTTP/2. Repro locally: cancel ctx mid-stream, goroutines stick around and connections show as active until TCP timeout. Anyone seen this pattern?

emma: yup saw that on a customer call. usually it's one of two things: 1) response body not closed, or 2) a custom RoundTripper wrapper swallowing the request context.

simon: I made sure we close resp.Body in our handler. still happens. stack traces show http2.readFrame or http2.(*clientConn).writeLoop blocked.

raj: can you paste the minimal client setup? specifically Transport settings.

simon: here's the client config I'm using:
```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  ForceAttemptHTTP2: true,
  MaxIdleConns: 100,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
  IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
req = req.WithContext(ctx)
resp, err := client.Do(req)
```

simon: repro: start a long streaming endpoint (server writes chunk every 1s), client starts read loop, then cancel ctx after 2s. server still thinks client connected for a long time. goroutines stack points to http2 framer.

olivia: two quick notes: 1) net/http's Transport will upgrade to http2 only if the server and TLS allow it; 2) golang.org/x/net/http2 has its own Transport that can be wired in and has extra timeouts (ReadIdle, PingInterval, PingTimeout). Might help detect dead peers faster.

raj: also check whether there's a proxy or connection pooling layer in between (e.g., our retry middleware). If that creates new Request objects without copying ctx, cancellation may not propagate.

emma: +1. We had a bug where our auth middleware did `req = req.WithContext(ctx)` but later wrapped req into a new http.Request via `http.NewRequest` and didn't transfer the context. That breaks cancellation.

simon: good point. our retry wrapper clones the request body for retries and uses `http.NewRequest(method, url, bodyCopy)` — didn't preserve ctx. I'll audit that.

raj: aside from context propagation, there are some http2 quirks: idle pings, stream resets. Consider enabling the http2 Transport's `ReadIdleTimeout` so a stalled stream is detected sooner. Example config (approx):
```go
import "golang.org/x/net/http2"
ht := &http2.Transport{
  AllowHTTP: false,
  ReadIdleTimeout: 30 * time.Second, // detects dead connections
  PingTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: &http2TransportShim{HT: ht, Base: baseTransport}}
```
(we have a shim in repo to hook http2.Transport into net/http's RoundTripper)

olivia: Another common footgun: `resp.Body` reader. If the caller doesn't drain or close it, the http2 stream may hang. For streaming APIs we should provide a convenience helper that handles early cancel: `func ReadStream(ctx, resp) { go io.Copy(io.Discard, resp.Body) }` pattern or ensure Close on cancel.

simon: thanks. I also saw references that `Transport.IdleConnTimeout` interacts badly with long-lived http2 streams — lowering IdleConnTimeout can cause extra churn. For streaming endpoints we probably want higher IdleConnTimeout but Pair it with http2 read/ping timeouts so dead peers are detected.

emma: actionable: 1) simon audit retry/auth wrappers to ensure ctx is passed through when constructing new requests. 2) raj to prototype adding http2 read idle/ping defaults to our SDK transport shim and expose toggles. 3) olivia to draft small helper for stream-cancel patterns in SDK docs.

raj: I'll spike the http2 Transport config today. I can add a unit + integration test that cancels ctx mid-stream and asserts connection/ goroutine cleanup within 5s.

simon: I'll open a PR to fix the retry wrapper if I find ctx leaks.

emma: I'll add a tiny example snippet in README and warn about cloning requests.

ci-bot: deployed test runner job queued: run/stream-cancel-leak-test (will report back logs). :gear:

olivia: one more debugging tip: use `net/http/httptrace` on the client to see connection reuse and `pprof` for goroutine stacks. Also `GODEBUG=http2debug=2` can be helpful.

simon: sweet — thanks all. I'll post findings here once I confirm root cause (likely ctx loss in our retry path)
